title: Socket effects precede whole-header writeback to user memory
mechanism: sys_recvmsg and send_mmsg_hdrs snapshot the whole user msghdr/mmsghdr, perform the socket effect, then write_val the entire saved structure back, touching input-only fields that Linux never writes.
contract: recvmsg writes back only msg_namelen, msg_controllen and msg_flags, and sendmmsg writes only msg_len, so input-only header fields are never overwritten and cannot cause a post-effect EFAULT (Linux net/socket.c).
observed: Source only: after the receive or send completes, the whole saved header is written back, so an unwritable input-only field yields EFAULT after the effect and concurrent input-field updates are reverted.

repro.how_to_run: No reproducer. finding.md Reproduction describes page-boundary placements of msghdr/mmsghdr with a read-only input-only part, controls on output fields, and a two-thread stale-overwrite check.

caveats: Source-only lead. Linux permits post-effect faults at contractual output fields, so those cases are controls. The UIO_MAXIOV part of CR-3 is AST-38.
